parole.testo: Formed from the Semitic root ק־ו־ה (“to collect”), related to the noun המים (“collection”). More at Mikveh.
Related to Classical Syriac ܦܛܘܪܬܐ (peṭṭōrtā) and Arabic فُطْرَة (fuṭra, “mushroom”), possibly loaned as a Semitic borrowing to French potiron (“pumpkin, winter squash”).

Common Semitic; see also Arabic قَامَ (qāma), Ge'ez ቆመ (ḳomä), Qatabanian [script needed] (*sqmt), [script needed] (*suqāmat, “planted”, literally “made to stand”), feminine passive causative adjective of [script needed] (*qāma, “to stand”). Possibly also related to שקמה (“sycamore tree”).
